reason: Pinned §5.2 leaves duplicate names unspecified and the raw counterexample parses as allow, although both current reference hosts use last-wins parsing and rejection requires a parser-level rule.
The framing ambiguity is confirmed at a4f546f, and the reference hosts' trim-based parsers make an explicit whitespace and BOM policy materially useful.
Stale retention and duplicate-list coverage gaps are confirmed, but uniqueness must follow §8's nonce-only identity and the retention work should be consolidated with the dedicated candidate.
Byte-for-byte comparison already excludes normalization, leaving malformed-Unicode handling and missing conformance cases as the defensible narrower finding.
The pinned hosts ignore consume_nonces in local mode, but a genuinely local verifier burns nonces and §3.2 permits omission when nothing needs burning, so blanket bare-allow rejection needs redesign.

Pinned §§3.2–3.4 impose no retention floor and existing vectors omit stale timestamps, supporting a bounded defensive clarification without establishing an exploit against the correct reference verifier.
The existing oversize vector requires oversize_stdout and independently proves process termination, so the claimed truncate-and-parse host would already fail rather than pass all 28 vectors.

Section 9 already requires effective-expiry rejection and the pinned verifier enforces it after delegation validation, while replacing credential expiry with leaf expiry changes signed semantics without a demonstrated conforming exploit.
Pinned §11 already defines optional-field evolution and its compatibility limitation, so the useful work is tightening that policy rather than asserting that no extension policy exists.

The published package is host-only, but the pinned repository already contains ten external_verifier vectors and a CLI runner at dist/main.js, so remaining cases should extend that machinery rather than invent an unsupported class.

Live [Datatracker status](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-chen-agent-decoupled-authorization-model/) identifies this draft as expired and archived, requiring terminal treatment under rule 2g rather than an active threat.

The [official changelog](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog) confirms the headers, but gateway demand, bundle provenance, and the proposed request-field mapping remain unproven.
The pinned IANA section already restricts registrations to versioned specification changes and explicitly declines a kind registry, directly contradicting the candidate's central allegations.
Pinned Appendix B explicitly disclaims normative wire obligations, and the receipts serializer cannot safely be relabeled JCS on the strength of one golden comparison.

Pinned architecture pseudocode checks exit before timeout and omits explicit schema, signal, and output-bound checks, making a bounded rewrite worthwhile despite the overstated lowercase-keyword argument.

The pinned draft already lists khandrew1 with its full commit, coverage, maturity, and implementation experience, while [RFC 7942](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7942#section-2) recommends some or all fields rather than requiring the asserted structure.

The hook seam exists, but [official timeout semantics](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#timeouts) distinguish fail-open command hooks from blocking SDK callbacks, undermining the proposed shell hook's claimed enforcement guarantee.

The [official transport specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports) supports header-based routing with body-authoritative validation, but adoption demand remains inferred and the existing mcp-use implementation is already server-side.

The [verified draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-chen-agent-decoupled-authorization-model-00) expired on August 18, 2026 and leaves its input contract undefined, requiring terminal status rather than the proposed active watch card.
The cited page could not be verified, independent authorship is unproven, and the actual ledger is empty rather than already containing implementation runs.
Pinned §§5.2–5.3 and the vector inventory confirm the gap, but Tier 2 must correct its checker allowlist because unparseable_stdout is already a valid spec token incorrectly rejected by that checker.

The proposed loop-run Cargo build writes under spec/reference-host-rs/target outside standards-autoresearch/, violating rule 2a, and its commands omit the host_behavior filter while the runner does not expose successful per-vector classifications.
The pinned 0.5.0 result and newer vector are verified, but the HUT command remains a placeholder and the template must remain staged until an actual successful run supports a ledger entry.
Pinned sync:check and independent hashes confirm local parity, but reproduction must hash JavaScript fixtures and distinguish vendored-source evidence from published-tarball verification.
